mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 2.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which may lead to increased borrowing costs and reduced consumer and business spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases when UNRATE < 5%, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects increased demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive economic growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the correlation between HOUST and S&P 500 forward returns is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year growth rate of GDP (GDPC1) exceeds the growth rate of CPI (CPIAUCSL), it indicates strong real economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of cases when GDPC1 growth > CPIAUCSL growth, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 112 indicates increased economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases when INDPRO > 112, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) reflects a strong labor market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the correlation between PAYEMS and S&P 500 forward returns is below 0.02 over a 2-year rolling window, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.2 percentage points and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it indicates potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE increases > 0.2pp and FEDFUNDS > 2%, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real disposable income (RSAFS) above $380 billion reflects increased consumer purchasing power, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases when RSAFS > 380000, the hypothesis is falsified.
